title: My Calendar II
statement:
Build a class `MyCalendarTwo` that accepts events one at a time. An event `[startTime, endTime)` occupies every real moment `x` with `startTime <= x < endTime`, so its end moment is not part of it. Two events may share time (a double booking), but no moment may ever be occupied by three accepted events.

- `MyCalendarTwo()` starts with an empty calendar.
- `book(startTime, endTime)` returns `true` and keeps the event if, with it added, no moment is shared by three accepted events. Otherwise it returns `false` and the event is discarded, so it never affects later calls.
constraints: At most 1000 calls are made to book
notes:
## Intuition

A new event is refused exactly when it touches a stretch of time that is already double booked. So besides the accepted events, keep the double-booked stretches themselves. Checking a new event against those stretches answers the question, and if the event is accepted, its intersections with the earlier events are precisely the new double-booked stretches. A brute force would instead count, for each start point inside the new event, how many accepted events cover it.

## Approach

1. Keep `bookings` (every accepted event) and `overlaps` (every stretch where two accepted events meet).
2. In `book`, scan `overlaps`: half-open intervals `[start, end)` and `[startTime, endTime)` intersect when `startTime < end && start < endTime`. Any hit means a triple booking, so return `false` without storing anything.
3. Otherwise scan `bookings`; for each one that intersects the new event, push the shared part `[max(start, startTime), min(end, endTime))` onto `overlaps`.
4. Push the new event onto `bookings` and return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

- `book(10, 20)` and `book(50, 60)` meet nothing: both stored, `true`.
- `book(10, 40)` hits no overlap, but meets `[10, 20)`, so `overlaps = [[10, 20]]`; `true`.
- `book(5, 15)` intersects `[10, 20)` in `overlaps` (5 < 20 and 10 < 15): `false`.
- `book(5, 10)` fails `10 < 10` against `[10, 20)`, so it is safe and meets no booking either: `true`.
- `book(25, 55)` misses `[10, 20)`; it meets `[50, 60)` and `[10, 40)`, adding `[50, 55]` and `[25, 40]` to `overlaps`: `true`.

Output: `[null, true, true, true, false, true, true]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) per `book`, where n is the number of accepted events: no moment lies in three events, so the stretches in `overlaps` never share a moment and number fewer than 2n. O(n²) over all calls.
- Space: O(n) for `bookings` and `overlaps`.

## Pitfalls

- Intervals are half-open: `[5, 10)` and `[10, 20)` do not intersect, so use strict `<` in both comparisons.
- Check `overlaps` completely before touching `overlaps` or `bookings`; a refused event must leave no trace.
- Store only the shared part of two events as an overlap, not either whole event.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bookings` | every accepted event as `[start, end]` |
| `overlaps` | every stretch already covered by two accepted events |
| `startTime`, `endTime` | the event being booked |
| `start`, `end` | the stored interval currently being compared |
